content: Aplasia cutis congenita (ACC) is the most common form of congenital cicatricial alopecia. It is characterized by a congenital, localized absence of the epidermis, which may or may not involve the deeper layers of the skin. Pathophysiology Genetics This dermatological condition has been associated with haploinsufficiency of the Peptidase D gene and a deletion on Chromosome 19. Associated Conditions ACC can occur in conjunction with several syndromes, including: Johanson-Blizzard syndrome Adams-Oliver syndrome Trisomy 13 Wolf-Hirschhorn syndrome Additionally, it has been observed in cases of in utero exposure to the antithyroid medications methimazole and/or carbimazole. Diagnosis Physical Examination The diagnosis of ACC is primarily clinical, based on the observation of characteristic skin findings.
